rv.q: In this revival, the lovely show turns out to be a soft-sell romance with enough charming open-road Americana to counteract its cornball plot and its passe message about the stigma of unmarried women.
Ravishing of voice and Olympian of stature, she’s an overwhelming presence in an underwhelming show.
This revival of the 1963 musical based on N. Richard Nash's play 'The Rainmaker' is a sweet-natured but dramatically inert evening that never generates the heat suggested by its title.
Only Ms. McDonald can make such awkward pronouncements as “My dreams are very plain, but nonetheless they’re very real” seem poignant and truthful.

cn.t: McDonald's luminous performance elevates this modest, threadbare 1963 musical beyond its limitations. Critics praise her ravishing vocals and affecting characterization, though most find the show itself underwhelming and gentle to a fault.

vs.sum: The legendary former nightclub retains a distinctive atmosphere even in its theatrical configuration. However, comfort is among the worst on Broadway — the rear mezzanine is extremely steep with limited guardrails and tight legroom throughout both levels.

acc.note: No elevator to Mezzanine. 10 induction loops. 81 assistive listening devices. Orchestra wheelchair seating.
